flag.name: Flag of the United States
flag.description: Thirteen horizontal stripes, alternating red and white, with a large blue rectangle in the canton bearing fifty small, white, five-pointed stars arranged in nine offset horizonal rows, where rows of six stars alternate with rows of five stars.
flag.symbolism: White is said to signify purity and innocence, red is said to signify hardiness and valor, and blue is said to signify vigilance, perseverance, and justice. Thirteen horizonal stripes represent the 13 original colonies, and fifty stars in constellation represent the fifty states of the Union.

oath of allegiance.name: Pledge of Allegiance
oath of allegiance.oath: I pledge allegiance to the Flag of the United States of America, and to the Republic for which it stands, one nation under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.

seal.name: Great Seal of the United States
seal.description: Obverse: the national coat of arms of the United States. Reverse: a truncated pyramid topped by an Eye of Providence, with the year 1776 noted in Roman numerals at the base of the pyramid, above the words *Annuit cœptis* and below the words *Novus ordo seclorum*.

coat of arms.name: Coat of Arms of the United States
coat of arms.heraldicDescription: Arms: Paleways of 13 pieces, argent and gules; a chief, azure; the escutcheon on the breast of the American eagle displayed proper, holding in its dexter talon and olive branch, and in his sinister a bundle of 13 arrows, all proper, in his beak a scroll, enscribed with this motto: "*E pluribus unum*." Crest: over the head of the eagle, which appears above the escutcheon, a glory, or, breaking through a cloud, proper, and surrounding 13 stars, forming a constellation argent on an azure field.

mottos.translation: A new order of the ages

symbols.creed: I believe in the United States of America, as a government of the people, by the people, for the people; whose just powers are derived from the consent of the governed; a democracy in a republic; a sovereign Nation of many sovereign States; a perfect union, one and inseparable; established upon those principles of freedom, equality, justice, and humanity for which American patriots sacrificed their lives and fortunes. I therefore believe it is my duty to my country to love it, to support its Constitution, to obey its laws, to respect its flag, and to defend it against all enemies.

flags.name: Flag of the United States Army
flags.description: A blue replica of the War Office Seal  set on a white field. Beneath the seal is a broad scarlet scroll bearing the inscription in white letters, "UNITED STATES ARMY." Beneath the scroll in blue sans serif Arabic numerals is "1775."
flags.symbolism: 1775 represents the year in which General George Washington was appointed as General of the Continental Army.

flags.name: Field Flag of the United States Army
flags.description: A white replica of the War Office Seal set on a blue field. Beneath the seal is a broad white scroll bearing the inscription in scarlet letters, "UNITED STATES ARMY." Beneath the scroll, in white sans serif Arabid numberals, is "1775."
flags.symbolism: 1775 represents the year in which General George Washington was appointed as General of the Continental Army.

flag.name: Flag of the United States Marine Coprs
flag.description: A centered Eagle, Globe, and Anchor on a scarlet background, with a streaming banner underneath bearing the words "UNITED STATES MARINE COPRS" in scarlet lettering.
flag.symbolism: The Corps emblem in gray and gold represents power on land, sea, and air. The design references the Continental Marines and the United Kingdom's Royal Marines.

seal.name: Seal of the United States Marine Coprs
seal.description: Standing upon the western hemisphere of the terrestrial globe containing the lines of latitude and topographical outlines of North, Central, and South America, an American bald eagle with wings displayed horizontally and inverted holding his beak in a scroll inscribed with the motto "SEMPER FIDELIS", all bronze. Behind the western hemisphere a foul anchor bend sinister-wise with stock, arms, and flukes in slight perspective, all bronze, on a scarlet background and within a dark blue band edged in gold circumscribed by a gold rope rim and inscribed "DEPARTMENT OF THE NAVY • UNITED STATES MARINE CORPS" in gold letters.

emblem.name: Eagle, Globe, and Anchor
emblem.description: Globe in silver showing the continents of the Western Hemisphere intersected by a fouled anchor with silver rope, and surmounted by a spread eagle, all in gold. In the eagle's beak a ribbon bearing "Semper Fidelis."

navy_master_chief_petty_officer.title: Master Chief Petty Officer of the Navy

mottos.translation: Not for self but for country

flags.name: Flag of the United States Navy
flags.description: Dark blue field. In the center of the flag is the inner pictoral portion of the seal of the Department of the Navy in its proper colors within a circular yellow rope edging above a yellow scroll inscribed "UNITED STATES NAVY" in dark blue letters.
flags.symbolism: The seal of the Department of the Navy represents naval heritage, readiness, and power on the seas. Gold rope represents tradition and cohesion.

flags.name: Union Jack of the United States
flags.description: 50 white five-pointed stars defacing a blue field in 9 rows, alternating between 6 and 5 stars (top to bottom), or 11 rows alternating between 5 and 4 stars (left to right).
flags.symbolism: Essentially the canton of the national flag, the jack represents the 50 states representing the Union.

flags.name: First Navy Jack
flags.description: 13 horizontal stripes of alternating red and white, charged with a rattlesnake and inscribed on the lowest white stripe: "DONT TREAD ON ME."
flags.symbolism: A historic maritime flag, the First Navy Jack symbolizes American independence, unity, and readiness to strike against tyrrany. The rattlesnake referrs to Benjamin Franklin's 1754 "Join, or Die" cartoon, while the motto is a warning to those who would encroach upon liberty or oppress freedom. The First Navy Jack replaces the Union Jack on the oldest navy-held ship with continual commission.
